issues.title: [Feature Request] Add configurable `fallback` (display name) option in `enchantmentSettings.json` for vanilla clients
issues.body:
### Problem Description

On vanilla Paper/Purpur servers, players connect using vanilla Minecraft clients without installing client-side mods or custom server resource packs.

In Minecraft 1.21+, custom enchantment descriptions rely on `Component.translatable(key, fallback)` in the generated datapack:
```json
{
  "description": {
    "translate": "enchantment.veinminer_enchantment.veinminer",
    "fallback": "Veinmine"
  }
}

Since vanilla clients do not have the custom translation key enchantment.veinminer_enchantment.veinminer locally, Minecraft's client-side renderer will always fallback to displaying the "fallback" value.

Currently, the "fallback" value is hardcoded as "Veinmine" inside EnchantmentPack.generate(), and enchantmentSettings.json does not provide an option to configure it. Because of this, server owners running non-English communities (e.g. Chinese, Spanish, German, etc.) cannot localize the enchantment name unless they manually decompile and patch the JAR/class files on every single plugin update.

Suggested Solution

Please consider adding a configurable display name / fallback string option in enchantmentSettings.json, for example:
{
  "displayName": "Veinmine",
  "minCost": 15,
  "maxCost": 65,
  "anvilCost": 7,
  "pickaxeOnly": false
}

When EnchantmentPack.generate() constructs data/veinminer_enchantment/enchantment/veinminer.json, it can use this value as the "fallback" attribute:
builder.put("translate", "enchantment.veinminer_enchantment.veinminer")
builder.put("fallback", settings.displayName ?: "Veinmine")

Benefits
Non-English Server Friendly: Server administrators can easily localize the enchantment name directly in the config file without forcing players to download resource packs.
True Vanilla Compatibility: Vanilla clients will immediately see the localized enchantment name in enchantment tables, anvils, and item tooltips.
No Jar Patching Required: Eliminates the need for server owners to bytecode-patch the plugin after each release.

Thank you for maintaining this great project!

issues.title: Migrate legacy configs: upgrade explicit tool lists to tags (so new vanilla tools keep working)
issues.body:
**What happens**

If a `groups.json` is carried across Minecraft/mod versions, its `tools` lists stay exactly as they were when the config was first generated. Configs from before tag support contain explicit item IDs:

```json
"tools": ["minecraft:wooden_pickaxe", "minecraft:stone_pickaxe", "minecraft:golden_pickaxe", "minecraft:iron_pickaxe", "minecraft:diamond_pickaxe", "minecraft:netherite_pickaxe"]
```

New versions ship a `default_groups.json` that uses tags instead (`#minecraft:pickaxes`), but that file is only used when `groups.json` is missing. This is not an exotic hand-edited config: the previous default (before #62) was an explicit list itself, so every config generated before tag support has this shape, and configs are rarely regenerated. In `BaseConfigManager.loadGroups()` an existing file is only rewritten when it contains *invalid* entries — a newly added vanilla tool like `minecraft:copper_pickaxe` is valid, it is simply absent from the list, so nothing happens and veinmining silently does not trigger for it.

Repro: carry a pre-tag `groups.json` into a newer version → mine an ore vein with a copper pickaxe → nothing happens.

This is the same symptom as #107 ("Copper Pick doesn't work with Veinminer"). The workaround suggested there — delete `groups.json` and let it regenerate — also throws away user-defined groups and block lists (I have a hand-made Wood group, for example). The same thing will happen again the next time a tool material is added.

**Request**

Migrate legacy configs on load, without discarding customizations. Ideas, roughly from least to most invasive:

1. When a group's `tools` list matches a known legacy default list exactly, replace it with the corresponding tag (e.g. the six pickaxes above → `#minecraft:pickaxes`). Only exact matches are touched, so custom entries are safe.
2. Add a `configVersion` field and migrate stepwise.
3. A user-triggered command or Mod Menu button ("update group tools") that rewrites only the tool entries of existing groups.

Option 1 looks like the smallest change that removes the silent part. Happy to open a PR for it if that is a direction you would take.

**Environment**

- Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Veinminer 2.12.2 (Fabric)
- Config carried over from an earlier instance; `groups.json` had the explicit pickaxe list while the jar's `default_groups.json` has `#minecraft:pickaxes`

issues.title: [Bug] Incorrectly penalizing chain excavations
issues.body: **Version** Applies to Datapack version 1.3.5 for Minecraft 26.2 **Phenomenon & Trigger Conditions** After using a tool configured under `veinminer:_config` to mine a block that is properly configured and enabled for veinmining, for the *first* time, any subsequent mining of *other* blocks that drop items – when done with the same tool near that veinminable block – will trigger veinmining on that originally configured block. **Example** - First mining stone does **not** trigger veinmining on diamond ore. - Mining diamond ore once triggers normal veinmining on diamond ore. - After that, placing diamond ore and stone again at the same location, and then mining stone a second time – **this will trigger veinmining on diamond ore**. **Root Cause** File: `function/internal/mine/_loopi.mcfunction` Line 5: `$execute if entity @s[scores={veinminer.b.$(namespace).$(id)=1..}] anchored eyes positioned ^ ^ ^1.5 at @n[type=item,nbt={Age:0s},distance=..5.0] run function veinminer:internal/mine/check_aligning` This line checks whether the player has mined that particular block type. However, after the veinmining chain finishes, the relevant scoreboard objective is **not reset to 0**. As a result, every time the player mines any block with that tool, the corresponding `veinminer.b.$(namespace).$(id)` score keeps increasing, causing veinmining for that block type to be triggered on every subsequent mining action with the same tool.

issues.title: Typo in veinminer.mcfunction - coal_depp should be coal_deep
issues.body:
## Bug Report - Typo in veinminer.mcfunction

**Datapack version:** 1.1.0  
**Game versions:** 1.17–1.20.2

---

### Issue location
`\data\veinminer\functions\veinminer.mcfunction`

### Description
There is a typo in the function call for deepslate coal ore. The file `coal_deep.mcfunction` exists in the `miner` folder, but it is referenced incorrectly as `coal_depp` (with double "p").

### Current (buggy) line
```mcfunction
execute as @s[scores={mined_co_d=1..}] at @e[type=item,limit=1,sort=nearest,nbt={Age:0s}] positioned ~ ~ ~ run function veinminer:miner/coal_depp
```

### Should be
```mcfunction
execute as @s[scores={mined_co_d=1..}] at @e[type=item,limit=1,sort=nearest,nbt={Age:0s}] positioned ~ ~ ~ run function veinminer:miner/coal_deep
```

### Result

issues.title: [Paper plugin] v2.10.1 incompatible with Minecraft 26.1.x / Paper 1.21.8+ (NoSuchFieldError + NoClassDefFoundError)
issues.body:
## [Paper plugin] v2.10.1 incompatible with Minecraft 26.1.x / Paper 1.21.8+

**Modrinth version:** v2.10.1 (paper) — the latest paper release
**Minecraft:** 26.1.2 (Purpur 26.1.2 build 2591)
**Client:** Fabric Loader 0.19.3 + `veinminer-fabric-2.10.3.jar` (sha1 `35b4f7ca72e9c105c028633b53c36fb8dc075eca`)

### Symptom

- Client-side chat shows on every join:
  ```
  Veinminer Disabled
  This server does not have Veinminer installed
  or disallowed the client addon
  ```
- Vein-mining never happens, even on Ores (the default group).
- The client-side hotkey addon still works (toggle key, wireframe highlight) — only the server-side decision / chain-break is broken.

### Server log (Purpur 26.1.2 build 2591)

```
[Server thread/INFO]: [Veinminer] Bigzhangbig joined with Veinminer version 2.10.3
[Server thread/WARN]: [Veinminer] Plugin Veinminer v2.10.1 generated an exception whilst handling plugin message
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: net/minecraft/resources/ResourceLocation
    at de.miraculixx.veinminer.networking.PaperPlatformNetwork.sendS2C(PaperPlatformNetwork.kt:37)
    at de.miraculixx.veinminer.network.NetworkRouter.sendConfiguration(NetworkRouter.kt:96)
    at de.miraculixx.veinminer.networking.PaperServerCallbacks.onJoinAccepted(PaperServerCallbacks.kt:39)
    ...
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation

[Server thread/ERROR]: Could not pass event BlockBreakEvent to Veinminer v2.10.1
java.lang.NoSuchFieldError: Class org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute does not have member field 'org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute PLAYER_BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED'
    at de.miraculixx.veinminer.VeinMinerEvent.removeAttribute(VeinMinerEvent.kt:317)
    ...

[Server thread/ERROR]: Could not pass event BlockDamageAbortEvent to Veinminer v2.10.1
java.lang.NoSuchFieldError: Class org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute does not have member field 'org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute PLAYER_BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED'
    at de.miraculixx.veinminer.VeinMinerEvent.removeAttribute(VeinMinerEvent.kt:317)
    ...
```

The `BlockBreakEvent` / `BlockDamageAbortEvent` exceptions fire on **every** block-break attempt by **every** player, not just chain-mining attempts.

### Root cause

Two API renames that landed between Paper 1.21.7 → 1.21.8 (carried through to 26.1.x):

| Symbol v2.10.1 references | Actual symbol in 26.1.x Paper API |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute.PLAYER_BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED` | `org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute.BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED` |
| `net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation` | `net.minecraft.resources.Identifier` |

Confirmed via the official Paper/Purpur API javadoc:
- Paper 1.21.1: `Attribute.PLAYER_BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED`
- Paper 1.21.8: `Attribute.BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED` (renamed)
- Paper 26.1.1-alpha: `Attribute.BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED`
- Purpur 26.1.2 build 2587+: `Attribute.BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED`
- `net.minecraft.resources.Identifier` exists in `purpur-26.1.2.jar` (11634 bytes at `net/minecraft/resources/Identifier.class`); `ResourceLocation` does not.

### Impact

1. The `NoClassDefFoundError` on `sendS2C` kills the S2C `Configuration` packet that tells the client "this server has Veinminer". The client then disables itself with the "Veinminer Disabled / This server does not have Veinminer installed" message — even though the server *does* have it.
2. The `NoSuchFieldError` fires on every `BlockBreakEvent` / `BlockDamageAbortEvent`, so even without the handshake issue, the listener chain can't decide whether to chain-break.

### Notes for maintainers

Your `gradle.properties` on `main` already has:
```
gameVersion=26.1
paperVersion=26.1.1.build.+
```
So you already migrated the build config to 26.1.x. The fabric side got republished as v2.10.3 (2026-06-04) but the paper side is still on the 1.21.x-compiled v2.10.1 (2026-05-29). A paper-side v2.10.2 / v2.10.3 with the two renames (`Attribute.BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED` in `VeinMinerEvent.kt:317`; `net.minecraft.resources.Identifier` in `PaperPlatformNetwork.kt:37` and its callsites) would fix it.

### Workaround for users until a paper-side release lands

Run Fabric Loader on the Purpur server. Drop in `fabric-api`, `fabric-language-kotlin`, and `veinminer-fabric-2.10.3.jar` into the server's `mods/` folder. Keep `veinminer-paper-2.10.1.jar` in `plugins/` (it will still throw the two errors, but Fabric takes over the chain-break decisions on the join S2C packet and it Just Works).

### How to reproduce

1. Install Purpur 26.1.2 build 2591 (or any 26.1.x build — confirmed build-independent).
2. Drop `veinminer-paper-2.10.1.jar` into `plugins/`.
3. Start the server with Java 25.
4. Connect with Fabric Loader 0.19.3 + `veinminer-fabric-2.10.3.jar` on the client.
5. Try to mine any block in survival — observe the client-side warning and the two server-side exceptions.

issues.title: [Suggestion] Support relative-position filters in group definitions for directional mining control
issues.body:
## Summary

Please consider adding relative-position filtering to Veinminer group definitions.

## Environment

* Veinminer version: 1.21.11
* Platform: Fabric

## Use case

A common use case is applying veinmining to shovel-compatible blocks while limiting traversal based on position relative to the source block.

One example is allowing connected blocks only when their Y coordinate is equal to or higher than the initial broken block.

Examples:

* allow `targetY == sourceY`
* allow `targetY > sourceY`
* disallow `targetY < sourceY`

## Current limitation

The current public configuration examples show grouping by block IDs and tools, but do not appear to provide a way to restrict traversal by relative position.

With the current structure, a group can target blocks such as dirt-like or shovel-compatible blocks, but it cannot distinguish between blocks above, at, or below the source block.

## Why this would be useful

Without a relative-position filter, connected blocks may also be mined below the starting point.
This makes some terrain-shaping and surface-clearing use cases harder to control.

## Suggested config direction

To preserve the current simple structure and avoid changing the format of `blocks`, an additional field at the same level as `blocks` and `tools` may be easier to maintain and extend.

For example:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Shovel Blocks",
    "blocks": [
      "minecraft:dirt",
      "minecraft:grass_block",
      "minecraft:coarse_dirt",
      "minecraft:podzol",
      "minecraft:rooted_dirt",
      "minecraft:gravel",
      "minecraft:sand",
      "minecraft:red_sand",
      "minecraft:clay"
    ],
    "tools": [
      "minecraft:wooden_shovel",
      "minecraft:stone_shovel",
      "minecraft:iron_shovel",
      "minecraft:golden_shovel",
      "minecraft:diamond_shovel",
      "minecraft:netherite_shovel"
    ],
    "conditions": {
      "relativePosition": {
        "minY": 0
      }
    }
  }
]
```

This would keep the structure flat and consistent:

* `blocks`
* `tools`
* `conditions`

A similar field name such as `filters`, `requirements`, or `predicates` could also work.
The main idea is to support traversal constraints without replacing the current string-based `blocks` format.

## Reproduction / use case

1. Define a veinminer group for shovel-compatible blocks.
2. Restrict the group to shovel items.
3. Break a target block near the surface.
4. Nearby connected blocks are veinmined.
5. Blocks below the source block cannot currently be excluded through config.

## Additional note

This is a feature request for more precise traversal control in group definitions, not a bug report about current veinmining behavior.

issues.title: [Suggestion] Support block-state filters in group definitions for crop maturity

## Summary

Please consider adding block-state filtering to Veinminer group definitions.

## Environment

* Veinminer version: 1.21.11
* Platform: Fabric

## Use case

A common use case is applying veinmining to crops with hoes while limiting the behavior to fully grown crops only.

Examples:

* wheat only when `age=7`
* carrots only at max age
* potatoes only at max age
* beetroots only at max age
* nether wart only at max age

## Current limitation

The current public configuration examples show grouping by block IDs and tools, but do not appear to provide a way to filter by block state.

With the current structure, a group can target `minecraft:wheat`, but it cannot distinguish immature crops from mature crops.

## Why this would be useful

Without block-state filtering, veinmining crop blocks also affects immature crops of the same block type.
This limits the usefulness of crop harvesting groups.

## Suggested config direction

To preserve the current simple structure and avoid changing the format of `blocks`, an additional field at the same level as `blocks` and `tools` may be easier to maintain and extend.

For example:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Wheat",
    "blocks": [
      "minecraft:wheat"
    ],
    "tools": [
      "minecraft:wooden_hoe",
      "minecraft:stone_hoe",
      "minecraft:iron_hoe",
      "minecraft:golden_hoe",

      "minecraft:netherite_hoe"

  }
]
```

This would keep the structure flat and consistent:

* `blocks`
* `tools`
* `conditions`

A similar field name such as `filters`, `requirements`, or `predicates` could also work.
The main idea is to support additional matching rules without replacing the current string-based `blocks` format.

issues.title: Veinminer drops loot from protected blocks without breaking them
issues.body:
When a player attempts to mine a block affected by Veinminer inside a protected region (e.g., using WorldGuard or Towny), the block is not broken — as expected — but it still drops its loot, allowing players to obtain resources from blocks that should be protected.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Set up a protected area using WorldGuard or Towny where players cannot break blocks.
2. Enter the protected region as a player without build permissions.
3. Attempt to mine a Veinminer-compatible block (e.g., an ore).
4. The block will not break, but the corresponding item drops anyway.

**Expected Behavior:**

- Protected blocks should not drop loot if they cannot be broken.

**Additional Info:**

- Protection plugins: WorldGuard and Towny
- Veinminer version: 2.4.4
- Veinminer version: 2.2.2
- Server type: Paper
- Minecraft version: 1.21.4

issues.body:

issues.title: [Feature] Add (Configurable) option for more levels
issues.body:
Hello!

It would be cool if we could have config options for more levels, which could then check conditionally for certain groups of blocks that only said levels can mine.

This would help bridge the gap between having tools mine all blocks, vs only specific ones. For example if a player wants their pickaxe to only have safer veinmining, ie ores only, they would enchant to only Veinmine I, while Veinmine II on that server could be configured to mine also stones, terracotta, more general blocks.

issues.title: Mod for 1.20.1 was compiled with Java 21
issues.body:
Veinminer 2.0.7 should not have been compiled with Java 21 because 1.20.1 uses Java 17.

While users can run 1.20.1 with Java 21 without issue, they should not have to do so.

Users can downgrade Veinminer to [2.0.4](https://modrinth.com/datapack/veinminer/version/2.0.4) so perhaps 2.0.7 should not be marked as being for 1.20.1

issues.title: Feature Request: Block Exchanger
issues.body:
Would you consider adding a new feature/enchant that could perform block exchanging? Basically it breaks the blocks the same way veinminer does but then replaces the blocks it breaks with a chosen block from the player's inventory. Have the user right click (+ hotkey) the block type they want to replace with using the tool, then they break the blocks the same way as vienminer.  Additionally would be nice to allow for different patterns like "surface only" that only breaks and replaces blocks that are adjacent to a transparent or air block. 

So I realize this probably be stretching the goals you have for this but I also feel this does sort of fit within the same sort of utility. I know there are other mods out there that can do this but they require client side mods, where as your veinminer can work server only. I think it would be great if it can be tied to a tool type and use the tools durability instead of other "power" sources or items that those other mods introduce.

To be honest Id also love to have a "builder's wand" style utility where you pick a pattern and choose a block and have it auto place. (Same as the exchanger but with "air" blocks)

issues.title: Durability is broken
issues.body: I can't speak for the other versions of the plugin/mod (fabric, etc.), but I am using the paper version on my server and when I break a vein (could be as small as 3 blocks) it will take like 100 durability from my pick. I think it is because you are not damaging the tool whenever a block is broken, but instead you're damaging it on every iteration, so it will take 1 durability away for every neighbor of the ore block and the ore block itself.
